findings: l.1436-1438: « Le noyau de V est vide, sauf si W est l'enveloppe convexe d'un point de H̊ et de W ∩ h » is true as an equivalence: the converse (not printed) holds too, since the rays of {s(−p) + w | s ≥ 0, w ∈ F(W) ∪ {O}} prolong W when W is the hull of p ∈ H̊ and W ∩ h (noyau_sature_nonempty_iff_isLeast)

l.1436-1438: the uniqueness of the apex needs only noyau W = ∅ (apex_unique); the existence of the greatest prolongation needs only W convex (isGreatest_sature), no closedness, no noyau hypothesis, no W ⊆ H
proof 3° (l.1471-1481): Zorn is unnecessary; the union of all prolongations is already a prolongation by 1° (two of its points lie in one prolongation)
questions: « l'enveloppe convexe » on S(E) read as the least convex part containing the set (IsLeast); on S(n) it is Benzecri.enveloppeConvexe (isLeast_iff_eq_enveloppeConvexe). Standard reading, no OQ

instances: Benzecri.prolonge_self: every convex part prolongs itself (instance of Déf. 1)
Benzecri.arcY_hypotheses: arcY = {y ≥ |x|} ⊆ S(1), H = {y ≥ 0} (formY) satisfies every hypothesis of Prop. 1 (generic case)
Benzecri.noyau_sature_arcY: the noyau of its saturated convex is empty
Benzecri.arcY_corps_convexe: arcY is a convex body of S(1), and so is its saturated convex (instance of the Corollary, hypothesis proved: arcY_ne_enveloppeConvexe)
Benzecri.ptY_hypotheses: the point (0,1) satisfies Prop. 1's hypotheses and is the exception (hull of itself and W ∩ h = ∅); the noyau of its saturated convex is nonempty
kb_proposals: Chapter3/Sature: sature l W := ⋃₀ {V | Prolonge l W V} is the greatest prolongation without Zorn (isGreatest_sature); its 1° works on any S(E) via ofCone (F V₁ ∪ {O} + F V₂ ∪ {O}) (prolonge_join), so enveloppeConvexe (S(n) only) is needed only to state the printed form
On S(n), IsLeast {k | IsConvexPart k ∧ A ⊆ k} W ↔ W = enveloppeConvexe A (isLeast_iff_eq_enveloppeConvexe): state hull conditions on S(E) with IsLeast and transfer through it
isConvexPart_ofCone: the rays of a convex IsPosCone containing O form a convex part — the cheap way to produce a convex part from a cone description
A closed part B of S(E) contains X when X + tY ∈ F(B) for all t > 0 (mem_F_of_forall_add_smul, through F_closure): the trace lemma inter_closedHemisphere_subset follows
rw [add_comm] on a goal over Fin (n + 1) → ℝ can rewrite n + 1 itself (motive not type correct): give the arguments, add_comm a b
